doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Musicians union, Actors Fund and relief grants
summary: The Federation of Musicians, Emergency Relief Fund, Actors Fund, Coda grants and the Jazz Foundation of America.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Right. Is the Musicians Union involved in any kind of support for their members?

They’re trying. The Federation, the overall Federation, the union that’s for the whole country of which local unions are part of that federation, it kind of sounds like the federation of planets. Star Trek. I wonder what the prime directive of the Federation of Musicians is.
Something like, “find a gig, damn it.”

That’s it. Prime directive. And so there is a thing called the Emergency Relief Fund which is helping some people. And this is something I hope your listeners hear this, because this is really good to know. People in the performing arts, there’s something that our musicians union in New York City got involved with several years ago called the Actors Fund. And those are people you can go to to get some kind of help, even if it’s just moral support. But they know where things are and they’re really good. I go to some © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

of their — every year for setting up my Medicare and health insurance and things like that. So there are resources. There are grants available. I know Coda Magazine has been issuing some small grants. And there’s the Jazz Foundation of America is trying to help. And one other thing, this is not a musical answer, but if you’re having trouble with unemployment, like I tried online like crazy ‘cause just what’s called the Gig or 1099 Unemployment which has been brought into being, and the word Gig actually used to be used for all kinds of freelance work. That’s where it came from I found out.
I didn’t know that. I thought that was —
